data.exact_reserve_text: An overall improvement of GBP 18.6 million on prior years' provisions was experienced during the year. This is due to improvements of GBP 18.8 million on casualty reinsurance and GBP 1.1 million on marine reinsurance partially offset by a deterioration of GBP 1.3 million on property reinsurance.

prior_year_events.impact_description: An unusual winter storm, named Uri, hit Texas in February 2021 with snow and a severe freeze that caused around $15 billion of damage.
In August 2021 Hurricane Ida ... caused an estimated loss of around $40 billion.
The year finished with an unusual run of very late tornados in the US mid-west.
A wildfire in Denver in late December 2021 affected the year.

named_events.loss_description: In 2023, the total insured loss from SCS events was estimated to be $60 billion (with eighteen individual events each greater than $1 billion).
The Atlantic basin hurricane season was also above average from an activity point of view with twenty named storms; seven reaching hurricane status and three of those being major hurricanes.
An unusual winter storm, named Uri, hit Texas in February 2021 with snow and a severe freeze that caused around $15 billion of damage.
In August 2021 Hurricane Ida ... caused an estimated loss of around $40 billion.
The year finished with an unusual run of very late tornados in the US mid-west.
A wildfire in Denver in late December 2021.
Sadly the war in Ukraine continued to dominate headlines; Syndicate 6134 had limited exposure to Ukraine, Belarus, and Russia. These exposures have now expired.

The fragile period of middle-eastern peace was shattered in October 2023 with the Hamas attack on Israel. The syndicate does, however, have some very limited, exposure to a number of assets in Israel. These exposures will be reduced over time, should hostilities continue.

data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate recorded a net release on prior years' reserves in 2023, with an overall improvement of GBP 18.6m on prior years' provisions. This movement was driven by favourable development in casualty reinsurance (GBP 18.8m) and marine reinsurance (GBP 1.1m), partially offset by adverse development in property reinsurance (GBP 1.3m). Prior underwriting years impacted include those from 2019, 2020 and 2021, which were affected by multiple natural peril events (for example, Winter Storm Uri and Hurricane Ida in 2021).

data.data_quality_notes: Prior year development (GBP 18.6m improvement) taken from 'Movement in prior year's provision for claims outstanding' narrative (note 3). The note provides an explicit overall improvement figure but does not break out 'gross' vs 'net' wording; the phrasing is taken as gross movement per the note. Opening gross claims outstanding taken from the Statement of Financial Position (prior year comparative column). A gross claims development triangle is present and was used as a supporting source. Some industry event loss figures quoted in the narrative are industry-wide and not syndicate-specific; syndicate-level net impacts for named events are not quantified in the report.
